reason: The e2e suite was the only validator that proves the browser-to-proxy-to-backend chain and it ran nowhere but a developer's machine, because playwright.config disabled its webServer under CI and the chat specs needed a live model; with LLM_PROVIDER=test in place the composed stack the exception asked for can exist. After this change every push and PR boots the backend on the CI pgvector and redis services, migrates, seeds the test user, builds the frontend and runs the suite on chromium, uploading the report on failure, and the exception is expired.
risks: First CI run may surface a runner-only difference (next start in standalone mode, cookie behaviour, MCP probe timing); the uploaded report and backend log are the diagnosis
e2e is now on the ci-ok path and is the slowest job; a flaky spec blocks the aggregate signal, so retries stay at 2 on CI
rollback: git revert. Nothing lives outside the repository.
security_impact: The e2e job runs the backend with ENVIRONMENT=local, LLM_PROVIDER=test (fake model, no key, no tool calls), a per-run SECRET_KEY derived from the run id, and the deployment-managed MCP_SERVERS list pointing at hostnames that do not resolve on the runner (probed and skipped). COOKIE_SECURE=false is set only in this job so the auth cookies work over http://localhost under next start. No secret is stored; the seeded test user lives in a service container that dies with the job.
summary: Run the Playwright end-to-end suite in CI against a real backend on pgvector and redis with the fake LLM provider, and retire the playwright-not-in-ci exception
